Title: Passage 1: The Lighthouse Birds
Content: Thick mist from the ocean sprayed on the breeze as Aurora walked down the rickety boardwalk. In the distance, outlined against the frothy white waves of the sea, stood a large red lighthouse. Well, the color resembled a chewed piece of bubble gum now, long since faded and washed out from the sun. The wooden boardwalk leading to the building had seen better `text(days)`, too. Aurora didn’t mind — she’d journey anywhere to capture a good story.
“No wonder they want to tear this place down — it’s not exactly easy on the eyes,” her co-editor Harrison complained, sidestepping what was `text(once)` someone’s picnic lunch.

Aurora sighed as they drew closer to the lighthouse. “Honeydew Lighthouse used to be the most gorgeous place on Honeydew Key. Did you know they built it in `1920`? It’s over a `text(hundred years)` old.”

“What happened to it?” Harrison asked, eyebrows raised in disbelief. Aurora had to admit, looking at the lighthouse now, it was hard to believe it was ever a shining beacon of the community, attracting tourists for its unbeatable views of the sea.
“As the town grew, new tourist attractions popped up — there’s that outlet mall, and the miniature golf course. I guess people are more interested in those things,” Aurora said sadly.
“Can you blame them?” Harrison asked. “Miniature golf is awesome, and this lighthouse is, well . . .” He trailed off, clearly not wanting to hurt Aurora’s feelings.
Harrison’s disdain for the lighthouse only reminded Aurora of the email she’d received a few `text(days)` ago from the keeper of the Honeydew Lighthouse.

:ibox:Aurora,

I read all your news stories in the local paper. I ask that you write a piece imploring the city to reconsider tearing down Honeydew Lighthouse. It is a cornerstone of history, and it deserves to remain standing.

Best,
William Washington

She had walked out of her office after reading the email and walked down to the beach to think. The rough, sandy shore and salty air helped clear her mind. Whenever she was feeling stumped, the crystal blue water gave her clarity and reminded her why she so deeply loved Honeydew Key.

Pulling out her phone, she began researching ideas for how to save the lighthouse. She considered starting a petition or trying to get the lighthouse named a historic landmark. There was no guarantee that either of those approaches would be successful, however, and they would be time-consuming, dragging on for `text(months)`, if not `text(years)`. Aurora wasn’t sure she had that kind of time. They could save the lighthouse if there were endangered or protected animal species living there, but that seemed unlikely.

No, her best approach would be to talk to Mr. Washington in person and rally the town’s support. This is how she ended up dragging Harrison reluctantly down the boardwalk toward Honeydew Lighthouse. She now noticed Mr. Washington at the top, attempting to repaint the peeling sides. He waved to Aurora and Harrison before suddenly disappearing into the lighthouse. When the pair reached the base of the building, a small door swung open. “Thank you both for coming,” Mr. Washington said as he ushered them inside.

As the group climbed the creaking staircase, the trilling sound of birds echoed off the walls. “Since the city has allocated its budget to renovate the downtown area for tourists, there is no money for me to restore Honeydew Lighthouse.”
The sound of birds grew louder the higher they climbed, and Harrison showed Aurora a face that screamed, “Seriously? You want to save a place overrun by birds?”
“This lighthouse is the reason for the town. Before all this new technology, it was the only way to guide ships,” Mr. Washington explained proudly.
As they reached the top of the lighthouse, the source of all the bird noise came into view. About a `text(dozen)` white birds roosted around the ceiling, feathers ruffling in the ocean breeze.
“I recognize that bird,” Harrison said excitedly, “It’s a Roseate Tern — did you know that they’re endangered?”
Silence fell over the group as sudden realization dawned on Aurora.
“Harrison, you may not love this lighthouse, but you are a genius!”
“I am?” His nose scrunched in confusion, unaware of what he had done.
“I know how to write my news article. We can save Honeydew Lighthouse!”
